answer: The strongest lever is simple: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because lotus only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
